newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-LARRY BROWN NAMED COACH OF THE 76ERS*.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-LARRY BROWN NAMED COACH OF THE 76ERS*.

text.p: Larry Brown, who resigned five days ago as coach of the Indiana Pacers, was named coachk of the Philadelphia 76ers on Monday.
Terms were not disclosed, but Brown reportedly received a five-year deal worth $25 million and was given complete control of the basketball operation.
Brown, who becomes Philadelphia's fifth coach in the last six years, resigned as coach of the Pacers last Wednesday.
The Sixers fired coach Johnny Davis and general manager Brad Greenberg on April 20th after a 22-60 season.
Brown met with the Boston Celtics about their coaching vacancy last week but said on Saturday he was no longer interested in that job.

It is another remarkable landing for Brown, who has never been unemployed at the start of a season despite eight job changes in a career that began in 1973 with the Carolina Cougars of the old American Basketball Association.
Brown guided the Pacers to a 39-43 record in 1996-97, just his second losing season in 24 years as a coach. The Pacers, hit hard by injuries, missed the playoffs for the first time since 1989.

Brown's all-time NBA coaching record is 624-480. He was 229-107 in four seasons in the ABA and 177-61 in seven years at the college level, including a national championship with Kansas in 1988. His overall coaching record is 1,030-648.
